transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I feel like my mind is constantly spinning about work and I just can’t shut the worrying off, no matter what I’m doing. It has gotten to the point where it's starting to take over my life, and I really need some help learning how to manage it.
How many months have you been experiencing this persistent, uncontrollable worry most days of the week?
This constant worrying has been going on pretty steadily for a little over a year now. It started about a few months after I took over the larger regional sales team, and it just hasn't let up since.
Besides the constant worrying, have you been experiencing physical symptoms like muscle tension, restlessness, fatigue, or difficulty sleeping most days?

Yes, absolutely, and it's exhausting. I feel constantly revved up, like I've had way too much coffee, and I'm always fidgeting or bouncing my leg because I just can't relax my body. On top of that, I lie awake for over an hour replaying work conversations, and then I wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning unable to fall back asleep.
Do you find that your mind frequently goes blank, or do you feel unusually irritable and easily annoyed by others due to this constant stress?

My mind doesn't really go blank, but I have been incredibly irritable and easily annoyed lately. I find myself snapping at my husband over tiny things, like asking where his keys are, or getting defensive when my teammates joke about me constantly checking my phone. I always feel so guilty afterward because I know they don't deserve it, but I just feel so on edge.
Do you find that your muscles, particularly in your neck, shoulders, or jaw, feel tight or sore most days due to this tension?

I haven't really noticed specific muscle tightness or soreness in my neck, shoulders, or jaw. It's more of a general physical restlessness where I feel constantly revved up and fidgety, like I just can't relax my body enough to sit still.
Do you find that your constant worrying makes it difficult for you to focus on your daily tasks, or does it feel like your mind often goes blank when you are trying to concentrate?

My mind doesn't go blank, but it gets so crowded with running "what if" scenarios that it is incredibly hard to focus on my daily tasks. My manager has actually warned me about seeming scattered in meetings, and I get completely distracted even during my hobbies like cycling or volunteering.
Do you feel that your worry is primarily focused on your performance at work, or are you equally worried about other areas of your life like your health, finances, or family safety?

It is heavily focused on my work performance, like losing accounts, team quotas, and my boss's opinion, though it does spill over into worrying about how we'd pay our mortgage if my commissions drop. I don't really worry about my health or family safety, but the anxiety about work is so constant that it completely overshadows my hobbies and time with my husband.

When you think about these worries, do you feel like they are specifically tied to your job responsibilities, or do you feel a sense of dread or anxiety even on days when you are off work and have no professional tasks to complete?

They absolutely bleed into my days off, and I feel a constant sense of dread even when I don't have any active work to do. I just can't seem to "switch off" the anxiety, whether I'm trying to relax on the weekend, cook with my husband, or go for a bike ride. It's always there in the background, no matter what I'm doing.
